title: Thousands Demand Clean Water in Jalisco and Lemus Uses It to Repress Them
author: SinEmbargo Staff
content:
_This article by SinEmbargo staff originally appeared in the[October 11, 2026
edition of SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4885657/fuera-lemus-miles-
llenan-calles-de-guadalajara-para-exigir-agua-limpia-fotos/), an independent
Mexican digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, October 11 (SinEmbargo).—** The **mega-march** to demand clean
water in **Guadalajara** ,
[**Jalisco**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4884766/alfaro-se-da-la-gran-vida-en-
espana-aca-millones-con-agua-puerca-porque-los-engano/), ended this Sunday in
**clashes** between protesters and the State Police in front of **Casa
Jalisco** , where the officers used pressurized water and tear gas. After the
events, alleged **arbitrary arrests** and the **disappearance** of two
participants in the **mobilization** were also denounced.

The protest began around 11:00 a.m. at the **Glorieta de La Minerva** , from
where thousands of people advanced along López Mateos avenue toward the
official residence of **Governor Pablo Lemus Navarro** , where the **protest**
escalated.

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-10.jpg)The march for clean water stretched more than 1.4
kilometers between La Minerva and Casa Jalisco. Photo: Claudia Jurado,
courtesy of SinEmbargo

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-9.jpg)Users in the Metropolitan Area marched to demand a solution
to the murky, foul-smelling water. Photo: Claudia Jurado, courtesy of
SinEmbargo

The mobilization stretched more than 1.4 kilometers (km) between La Minerva
and the residence of the state executive, according to citizen reports.
Families, residents of different parts of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area
(ZMG), and other participants joined to protest the quality of the water that
reaches their homes.

With signs and chants, the protesters demanded a solution to the supply
problem, which has persisted for months.

Among the phrases heard were "Out, Lemus!", "We want clean water!" and "Water
is a right, not a privilege!"

The complaints were directed both at the Government of Jalisco and at the
[Intermunicipal System of Drinking Water and Sewerage Services
(SIAPA)](https://info.jalisco.gob.mx/dependencia/sistema-intermunicipal-de-
los-servicios-de-agua-potable-y-alcantarillado-siapa), the agency responsible
for the service in the Metropolitan Area.

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-6.jpg)"Water is a human right. It is not a privilege," reads one
of the signs at the march. Photo: Claudia Jurado, courtesy of SinEmbargo

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-8.jpg)Families and citizen collectives took part in the protest
over water quality. Photo: Claudia Jurado, courtesy of SinEmbargo

Other attendees carried signs with messages such as "Stop SIAPA corruption"
and "Water is a human right. It is not a privilege." They also chanted "The
people united will never be defeated!" to protest that the water they receive
in their homes is of poor quality.

The discontent had already been expressed days earlier at the Western
Institute of Technology and Higher Education (ITESO), where students
confronted Lemus and complained to him about the dirty water, insecurity, and
public transportation fares. During that encounter, the Movimiento Ciudadano
(MC) Governor promised that this Sunday's march would take place calmly.

## Arrests and Disappearances After Clashes at Casa Jalisco

According to a report by the newspaper _Reforma_ , the clashes began around
1:20 p.m. in front of Casa Jalisco, where protesters threw dirty water,
bottles, and sticks at state police officers.

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-7.jpg)Protesters advanced along López Mateos avenue toward the
Governor's official residence. Photo: Claudia Jurado, courtesy of SinEmbargo

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-3.jpg)The march demanded verifiable answers about water quality in
the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area. Photo: Claudia Jurado, courtesy of
SinEmbargo

The officers responded first with jets of pressurized water and then with tear
gas. However, the report noted that the gas also affected people who were not
taking part in the attacks, among them **children and older adults**.

> I've been going to marches since the nineties. I had never felt the risks I
> felt at today's. This is how Jalisco is [mis]governed.
>
> Academic Bernardo Masini, on his X account

The Palestine Solidarity Network Guadalajara released an urgent statement in
which it denounced that Eduardo Ramírez Silva and Ricardo Ramírez Silva had
allegedly been "picked up" by State Police officers one block from Casa
Jalisco during the mobilization.

> [Post by @redxpalesgdl on
> X](https://twitter.com/redxpalesgdl/status/2109366773610856583)

> [Post by @SinEmbargoMX on
> X](https://twitter.com/SinEmbargoMX/status/2109377244892209329)

The organization demanded the "immediate release" of both and asked that they
be "presented alive immediately," but so far the complaint does not detail how
it happened.

In another video circulating on social media, four young women denounced
having been detained in the vicinity of Casa Jalisco.

From there, they stated that they were dragged during their detention and that
they did not know where they would be taken.

> [Post by @SinEmbargoMX on
> X](https://twitter.com/SinEmbargoMX/status/2109379761533534588)

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-2.jpg)With signs and chants, residents demanded a clean and safe
supply. Photo: Claudia Jurado, courtesy of SinEmbargo

One of them appears with a head injury, while the others state that State
Police officers took their belongings, among them a cell phone and a pair of
glasses. They also held the officers responsible for anything that might
happen to them.

## Families Pay More for Bottled Water

Behind the protest are months of discontent over water quality in various
neighborhoods of the metropolis, where some residents report unusual coloring,
sediment, and foul odors, a situation that has forced some families to **buy
bottled water to cover basic needs**.

On October 5, residents also took their discontent to the streets with
blockades at various points of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area, among them
Periférico Sur and 8 de Julio avenue, López Mateos Sur, and the intersection
of Colón and Jaime Torres Bodet.

> [Post by @SinEmbargoMX on
> X](https://twitter.com/SinEmbargoMX/status/2109360012959133853)

> [Post by @SinEmbargoMX on
> X](https://twitter.com/SinEmbargoMX/status/2109362145439912232)

Although the Government of Jalisco announced measures to address the
situation, among them reducing the flow of water from the Las Pintas dam, this
Sunday's call went ahead.

In parallel, Governor Pablo Lemus shared testimonies on social media with
which he claimed that the water quality had begun to improve. However,
citizens maintain their demands and ask for results that can be verified in
their homes, as well as public information about the causes of the problem.

This Monday, SIAPA is expected to announce the neighborhoods where rationing
will be applied, as part of the measures to adjust the supply while the
situation is addressed.

> [Post by @SinEmbargoMX on
> X](https://twitter.com/SinEmbargoMX/status/2109364661993009276)

## Alfaro Lives It Up. Here, Millions With Filthy Water

Enrique Alfaro promised that Guadalajara would have guaranteed water for the
next 50 years. Two years later, while the former governor develops a new
career in Spanish soccer, residents of the Metropolitan Area open the tap and
receive black, murky water that smells "as if it had excrement."

The water crisis that his Administration bequeathed to his MC fellow party
member Pablo Lemus has now reached a critical point, and now, in addition to
the contamination, **hundreds of thousands of people will face months of
shortages**. Alfaro maintained in 2024 that the works carried out during his
Government secured the supply for five decades.

And so, people open the tap to wash the dishes and the water stinks. They get
ready to go to work, but they cannot bathe because it comes out black and
fetid, as recounted by Alejandro García, a resident of Zapopan, Jalisco.

> [Post by @SinEmbargoMX on
> X](https://twitter.com/SinEmbargoMX/status/2109375514553340374)

> [Post by @redxpalesgdl on
> X](https://twitter.com/redxpalesgdl/status/2109366542647328793)

It is the opposite of that promise by Alfaro: while Guadalajara today faces an
emergency due to contaminated water and a deteriorated supply system, the
former governor is in Valladolid, Spain, where after joining professional
soccer he ended up as Director of Organizational Development of Real
Valladolid.

## A Promise Into the Void

Alfaro certainly left a crisis that belies his claim of having guaranteed
water for the next 50 years. And his successor, Pablo Lemus, acted late in the
face of an emergency. Now the problem blew up on him, says Josué Daniel
Sánchez Tapetillo, a water resources specialist.

> "This is the result of many bad decisions, of the whims of previous
> governments," the engineer elaborates. With Enrique Alfaro "we lost six
> years and now we have dirty water up to our necks, literally." The former
> governor refused to build a necessary aqueduct and almost in his last year
> accepted the project, but never got it going.

> [Post by @Ferchiz_VR on
> X](https://twitter.com/Ferchiz_VR/status/2109379334905659730)

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-12.jpg)The water crisis forces families to spend more money on
buying water jugs. Photo: X @markos_f_f

Now Pablo Lemus "is forced to take action," he said, actions that come very
late and whose results will take several months, will leave the metropolitan
area without water, and will spend billions of pesos on a work that will serve
only for a while, only to spend again on the one that is truly needed: **a
second aqueduct at Lake Chapala**.

"I got close to her and she smelled like poop, freshly bathed and she smelled
like poop!" Luz Ramos's daughter bathed with the water that comes out of the
shower, the water supplied by the Intermunicipal System of Drinking Water and
Sewerage Services (SIAPA). She had to bathe again with water from a jug. Every
five days, recounts the 65-year-old woman from Guadalajara, they have to buy
six water jugs. Each month, they spend about 1,500 pesos.

## Why Is a Second Aqueduct Needed?

Enrique Alfaro was the first MC Governor in Jalisco. In his campaign, he
played at presenting himself as an alternative to the PAN and the PRI and at
seeming close to the citizenry. He championed the rejection of the second
aqueduct from Lake Chapala and promised that, if he came to power, he would
cancel that state project. And he won the elections for the 2018-2024 term.

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-11.jpg)Reports of alleged acts of repression added to the
discontent over the water crisis. Photo: X @BernardoMasini

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-4.jpg)Citizens questioned the State Police's conduct during the
protest. Photo: X @BernardoMasini

The general public, together with academia and specialists in water issues,
requested and recommended the construction of that second line of the Chapala-
Guadalajara aqueduct, explained Josué Daniel Sánchez Tapetillo.

Some groups in the municipalities near the lake were distrustful and feared
that this line would not be used as a substitute, but to extract more water.
But the thing is that Alfaro said the same, that they should not take more
water out of the lake. Although it was his decision not to extract more. "It
was a populist discourse, in reality he did not want to get into conflicts
with the people of the Lake Shore," says Sánchez Tapetillo.

The Guadalajara Metropolitan Area gets its water mainly from Lake Chapala,
which provides it with about 60 percent of the volume it consumes. The
resource arrives by two routes: a closed aqueduct and an old system of canals
with contamination problems.

![Residents of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area march to demand clean
water](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jalisco-clean-
water-march-5.jpg)Users urged answers from the authorities in the face of the
water crisis. Photo: X @BernardoMasini

The old system turned 70 years old; it was built in 1956. It provides from
2,000 to 2,500 liters per second, but it crosses urbanized areas where it
receives wastewater, industrial discharges, and possible agricultural
contaminants. That canal system diverts water toward a stretch of the Santiago
River and then toward the Atequiza canals, until reaching the Las Pintas dam.
From there it is pumped to the Miravalle No. 1 water treatment plant and then
distributed to the population of Guadalajara and the surrounding
municipalities.

The aqueduct was built in 1991; it is the most recent work to transport water
from Lake Chapala. And the flow it carries is much greater: between 5,000 and
5,500 liters per second, explains Josué Daniel Sánchez. Being closed, it
avoids the polluting discharges present in the canals along the route.

> "It is a single pipe and for that reason, practically, it has never received
> maintenance," because it would have to be shut down and it is the main water
> supplier, notes Sánchez Tapetillo. That is why "it was important to build
> this second complementary or substitute aqueduct."
